memory: I have Rs=20 Ω optimum at 0.00 mm. With a measured 42 ps edge, 250 mV into 50 Ω, and 50k averages I observed ≈0.08 nH per 0.25 mm; noise floor ≈±0.06 nH. Limiting factors are instrument jitter, thermal drift (~0.4 °C), and capacitive-coupling shifts when toggling the via fence. The per-mm inductance plus reduced capacitive coupling hypothesis remains plausible but unisolated. Plan: raise stimulus to 500 mV, increase to 100k averages, implement active thermal stabilization, perform paired-difference via-fence subtraction, and refine deconvolution algorithms.
openQuestion: Can a conductive guard ring (brass washer) around the via fence reduce capacitive coupling enough to reach ±0.05 nH with 500 mV/100k?
